T1.claim: DIY woodworkers will adopt Biesse machines if they perceive the machines as affordable, easy to use, and compatible with existing tools, because they value precision and time savings in their home projects.
T1.who_benefits: Individual DIY woodworkers who need accurate, repeatable cuts for furniture, cabinets, and other projects.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: If Biesse offers a compact, affordable CNC router that plugs into standard outlets and works with common wood materials, these users will purchase directly rather than relying on professional services.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Biesse captures value through direct sales of entry‑level machines, subscription services for software updates, and accessories, leveraging its existing B2B distribution channels to reach consumers.
assumptions: DIY woodworkers currently use hand tools or basic CNC machines for home projects.
Price sensitivity is a primary factor for this segment.
Biesse can produce a machine that meets DIY precision requirements without compromising professional‑grade quality.
predictions: In a test offering a €2,000 CNC router to 100 DIY woodworkers, at least 30% will purchase within 12 weeks.
Purchase intent will be higher when the machine is described as "easy to set up and use for home projects."
Willingness to pay will be above €1,500 for a machine that delivers repeatable accuracy.
T1.first_claim: DIY woodworkers will adopt Biesse machines if they perceive the machines as affordable, easy to use, and compatible with existing tools, because they value precision and time savings in their home projects.

T2.claim: Homeowners will adopt Biesse machines if they receive a subscription model that includes software updates, cloud storage, and remote support, because they value ongoing performance improvements and convenience.
T2.who_benefits: Homeowners who need reliable CNC machines for occasional projects and value low maintenance.
T2.why_behaviour_changes: A subscription model removes upfront purchase cost, provides access to new features, and ensures the machine stays up-to-date, making it attractive for infrequent users who prefer flexibility.
T2.how_value_is_captured: Biesse captures value through recurring subscription fees, data-driven insights from usage, and potential cross-selling of accessories and services.
assumptions: Homeowners currently use a mix of hand tools and basic CNC machines for DIY projects.
They are willing to pay a monthly fee for convenience and performance.
Biesse can deliver software updates remotely without compromising professional-grade quality.
predictions: In a test offering a subscription-based CNC router to 100 homeowners, at least 40% will subscribe within 12 weeks.
Subscription uptake will be higher when the model is described as "pay-as-you-go with automatic updates."
Monthly cost will be acceptable if it is under €50 and includes cloud storage and basic support.

X1.name: Subscription vs Entry-Level CNC Test
X1.method: Randomized controlled trial with two parallel groups. Group A receives a €2,000 entry-level CNC router with a limited warranty and optional accessories. Group B receives the same router plus a 12-month subscription that includes software updates, cloud storage, and remote support. Both groups are offered a 10% discount if they sign up for the subscription within 12 weeks. The test runs for 12 weeks, and participants are contacted weekly to assess purchase intent,
X1.sample: 200 DIY woodworkers recruited via woodworking forums, social media, and local workshops. 100 participants per group.
X1.measure: Purchase conversion rate (percentage of participants who buy the router) and subscription uptake rate (percentage of participants who subscribe to the service).

prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B subscription rate ≥ 40%, Group A subscription rate ≤ 20% (subscription model provides convenience and ongoing updates).

X1.decision_rule: If Group A purchase rate ≥ 30% and Group B purchase rate ≤ 15%, proceed with developing a differentiated consumer proposition around entry-level machines. final.value_proposition: A compact, affordable CNC router that plugs into standard outlets and works with common wood materials, delivering professional-grade precision without the professional price, sold through Biesse’s existing dealer network.
final.next_action: Run the proposed 12‑week randomized controlled test (Subscription vs Entry‑Level CNC Test) with 200 participants to measure purchase conversion and subscription uptake. Use results to decide whether to develop the entry‑level consumer line.
final.uncertainty: The size of the DIY woodworker market and their willingness to pay for an affordable CNC router are uncertain. The test will clarify demand and price sensitivity.
would_change_if: If the test shows Group A purchase rate ≥ 30% and Group B purchase rate ≤ 15%, proceed with the entry‑level consumer proposition. If Group B subscription rate ≥ 40% and Group A subscription rate ≤ 20%, consider a subscription‑based model.

result.title: Simulated small-workshop CNC software offer test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited owners of small carpentry workshops and skilled hobby woodworkers were assigned equally to two offers for the same compact CNC router. Both showed the identical machine, working area, price, installation, warranty and delivery time. One offer came with simplified design software and a library of ready-to-cut furniture templates that need no programming; the other came with the standard professional CAD/CAM software. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a paid refundable deposit remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 deposits for the template-software offer and 72 for the standard-software offer. This tests whether programming complexity changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that a machine at a price these buyers pay could be built, that the market is large enough, or that it fits the company's industrial dealers. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.

T1.how_value_is_captured: Nabtesco can charge a premium for bundled smart home-compatible automatic doors and welfare equipment, and sell directly to consumers, reducing reliance on distributors and increasing margin.

predictions: If Nabtesco launches a bundled smart home kit, purchase intent among target consumers will be at least 15% higher than for separate components.
